items: A new Report tab: a period report on this week, this month or the year to date, with a day map, a top harness / model / project podium, an hour-and-weekday rhythm, and a row per harness.
Two shareable cards at the foot of the Report tab, exported as 1080x1920 PNGs. Every export writes both a light and a dark card, and cost stays off until you ask for it.

Seven new style themes adapted from cosyncing: Teal Obsidian, Graphite, Nordic Warmth, Cyber Amber, Royal Navy, Soft Minimalist and Flat White, each with its own light and dark tokens, heatmap and chart palettes.

Antigravity sessions run through an ACP host are now counted. The antigravity-acp and antigravity-ide product homes are scanned alongside antigravity-cli, all reporting under the one Antigravity entry, and ANTIGRAVITY_HOME adds further homes without displacing the defaults.

A second Claude Code subscription now reaches the Quota tab. With credential scanning consented, every ~/.claude* install that has its own sign-in is polled, and the Claude card groups its windows by install under the directory name it was set up with.
gpt-6-astra is priced at OpenAI's published standard rates instead of showing as $0.
tokdash serve --dev-fixture dense now serves /api/insights, so the Report tab can be worked on against the fixture.

Theme defects across the style set: the refresh glyph and the select caret no longer disappear on light-buttoned themes, Overview KPI values no longer wrap in the monospace themes, Flat White panels have their separation from the page back, and label text that sat below WCAG AA contrast was corrected in nine theme and mode combinations.
The Report tab's panels follow the active style theme instead of painting a literal white or slate blue on every theme.

A quota card that measures two accounts no longer blames one of them for the other's failure. A failing MiniMax China plan reads as a problem with that plan rather than the healthy global one, and one region's recovery no longer leaves the other's stale error in place.

Low-quota alerts no longer go quiet on a working Claude install while a sibling install stays broken. A quota row's last-known marker and its alert eligibility now compare against the status of the account that owns the row.
A quota card now prints an error that belongs to none of the accounts it lists, instead of letting any account list silence it.
The multi-server views no longer count a working subscription as needing attention. A provider is OK when at least one of its accounts is healthy and the card's own error belongs to one of them.
tokdash serve --dev-fixture dense no longer answers /api/insights with a 500 for a short explicit date range.
Gemini 3.8 Flash, Tencent HY4 Preview and Muse Spark 1.3, plus the Muse Spark contributor tier, are priced instead of showing as $0.

Model names that matched nothing now resolve: the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next spellings price as Qwen3.8 Flash, gemini-3.7-flash-control as Gemini 3.7 Flash, and doubao-seed-code, doubao-seed-2.0-code and ark-code as Seed 2.0 Code.
Claude Fable 5.1 is priced, with fable-5.1 style aliases, instead of showing as $0.
tokdash serve --dev-fixture dense starts the dashboard against a dense synthetic dataset for UI work, reading none of your real history.

Refresh while a large Codex session is streaming no longer takes 30-60 s or balloons memory: the Codex and Claude parsers stream their logs, one sync runs per source at a time, and the comparison window reuses the current window's sync.
The first request after upgrading re-parses Codex session files once; on a large history that is a one-off pause of some tens of seconds.
Zed, Qwen Code and Charm Crush are new usage sources, read locally from each tool's own store.
WorkBuddy and Qoder IDE now have their own Session Explorer panels, with per-session turns and active time.
A new /api/insights endpoint returns hour-of-day, weekday, heatmap, per-project and streak analytics in one request.
Usage responses carry top_models_by_cost alongside the token-ranked top_models, and stats adds messages, most_used_model and highest_cost_model.
Model lists are ordered by tokens, as the API reference always described. The cost ranking is served separately rather than replacing it.
The favorite model ranks by tokens rather than cost, so a rarely used but expensive model no longer wins.
A project name is taken from the last element of a Windows path as well as a POSIX one, so the same project seen from Windows and WSL groups together.
Calendar heatmap days carry a real intensity instead of always zero, so the calendar shades again.
Current and longest streaks are computed instead of always returning zero.
Refresh no longer reports success while serving cached data.
Hermes named profiles are scanned by default, so usage kept under ~/.hermes/profiles/<name> no longer goes missing from Overview and Session Explorer.
Yesterday's figures are warmed just after midnight, so the first Yesterday click of the day is already cached.
The cap on concurrent heavy computes now scales with the CPUs this process may actually use, up to 8, instead of a fixed 2.
Switching to a date range nothing has computed no longer leaves most Sessions panels failing. Requests that cannot get a compute slot now queue briefly instead of being refused outright.

Yesterday and other past date ranges now recompute once the range has ended, instead of showing the partial figures cached while it was still in progress. Previously only the Refresh button corrected them.
Quota provider visibility menus now list the harnesses reported by their own server and keep every server block synchronized when the shared preference changes.
Added Japanese, Korean, Spanish, and Portuguese dashboard languages, with automatic browser-language detection and locale-aware dates and numbers.
Added opt-in Z.ai Coding Plan quota tracking for 5-hour, weekly credit, and legacy MCP windows.
Updated pricing data to 2.0.20 with 14 newly listed models.
Refresh reports now appear for every repeat refresh of the displayed range while respecting an explicit dismissal.
Session panels now show each harness's brand logo, and harnesses with no sessions in the selected range are hidden instead of rendering empty panels.
The first dashboard load after startup no longer returns a transient 503 while the cache warms.
Added Session Explorer support for Antigravity CLI, Cline, Grok Build, Hermes, Kilo Code, and omp, with per-turn usage and active time.
Added a Servers tab for comparing configured Tokdash instances and collapsible per-tool session panels.
Refresh now reports source-level additions, updates, removals, and unchanged rows from incremental scans.
Overview and session runtime cards now report agent time consistently, and unchanged source files are reused during rescans.
Fixed queued dashboard refreshes, stale date-range breakdowns, Antigravity WAL metadata invalidation, and Cline project fallback.
Added omp (oh-my-pi) as a local token and cost source, reading the same session format as Pi across the default tree, the init-xdg migration root, and named profiles.
Added Kilo Code as a local token and cost source, covering the CLI and the current VS Code extension through their shared store, including dev-channel databases.
Added Cline as a local token and cost source, reading per-session message files so subagent spawns are counted in full rather than dropped.
Added local omp, Kilo Code, and Cline brand marks throughout dashboard tool rows and charts.
Each scanned session directory is now claimed by exactly one source, so two clients pointed at the same tree can no longer count the same tokens twice.
The persistent store's cross-file stable-key sync is a declared parser capability instead of a Codex-specific branch, keeping the correct owner for Cline's forked session files.
Added WorkBuddy as a local token and cost source, with cache-aware prompt accounting and per-model pricing.
Added Qoder IDE and Qoder CLI as separate local usage sources, including authoritative provider-credit costs where Qoder reports them.
Added local WorkBuddy and Qoder brand marks throughout dashboard tool rows and charts.
Parser changes now invalidate only that parser's persistent usage cache, while pricing changes reprice stored rows without rereading source logs.
Native-Windows setup, re-setup, doctor, and uninstall now classify and stop owned processes safely while leaving foreign port holders alone.
Closed cache races that could expose mixed pricing generations or preserve stale costs after a concurrent sync.
Made Qoder fixture reads explicit UTF-8 so the parser suite passes on Windows consoles with legacy default encodings.
Added ZCode as a local token and cost source, with cache-aware input accounting and per-model pricing.
Added ZCode to the Session Explorer with turns, per-model billing, and measured active-time events.
Added Qwen3.8 27B pricing and ZCode branding across the dashboard and documentation.
Fixed native-Windows setup, locked-file session reads, and usage-database resync behavior.
Made ZCode live-database reads coherent and read-only at the source by querying disposable SQLite snapshots, with retry-safe caching.
Reasonix is now a tracked source. Tokdash reads its per-request stats and session logs from ~/.reasonix (or $REASONIX_HOME), pricing each provider/model pair through the usual pricing database.
Sessions can now use a step duration the tool measured itself rather than inferring one from the gap between events, so idle time between an answer and your next prompt is excluded outright.
Changing the date range no longer leaves the previous range's Apps & Models and Combined Models tables under the new range's label.
The Agent Time card now shows that it is loading instead of a dash, which read as “no agent time” while its request was still in flight.
Restored DeepSeek Harness session loading when the persistent usage database is disabled or unreadable.
Codex subagent and fork sessions no longer double-count the parent thread they replay — newer Codex writes forks in a shape the old check could not see.
Codex usage is no longer attributed to gpt-5.3-codex when a rollout records no model; those rows now take the file's own model, or read as unknown at zero cost.
Picking a date range no longer keeps a fork's replayed rows when the range excluded the parent session.
Codex rollouts moved to ~/.codex/archived_sessions are now read alongside the active ones, without counting anything twice.
Sessions spanning many files now load much faster. Claude splits one session across every subagent it spawns, and merging those rows was quadratic in the file count.

Added DeepSeek Harness (dsh) as a token, cost and session source — each step's early usage chunk folds into its finalized message, and a forked session's inherited prefix is skipped, so nothing is double-counted.
DeepSeek Harness sessions appear in the Session Explorer with title, project and active time, and sync into the persistent store.
Added GLM 5.3, DeepSeek V4 Pro and Grok 4.6 pricing, plus a DeepSeek Harness brand mark.
Updated the DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro rates to the current official prices.
Added an estimated agent time card to the Overview, with a change against the previous period.
Added estimated active and agent runtime to sessions and per-tool panels, with an idle cap so a session left open overnight no longer reads as an all-night session.
Added Kimi to the session explorer, including per-agent stream timing.
Cached session rows now hold their billing inputs and are priced when read, so editing a rate reprices immediately instead of reparsing every session log.
Kept the cost OpenCode and Mimo report themselves instead of replacing it with an estimate.
Stopped a superseded dashboard load from showing its results or its errors under the range you switched to.
Replaced the quick-range horizontal scrollbar with a responsive More ranges disclosure that keeps the selected preset visible.
Preserved persistent usage caches across unchanged package upgrades while retaining invalidation for pricing data and calculation changes.
Removed duplicate empty quota history panels from multi-server dashboard views.
Added a localized in-app What's new drawer and local brand marks throughout tool breakdowns.
Unified loading states, refined the Overview profile hierarchy, and kept quick date ranges compact on one row.
Enabled same-tailnet Tailscale Serve dashboards to combine Tokdash servers without manual CORS setup while keeping remote writes blocked.
Synchronized today's Profile Activity totals, removed duplicate tool-icon transfers, and kept long themed pages visually continuous.
Kept the Settings dropdown above dashboard cards in themes that use blurred surfaces.
Added multi-server selection across the dashboard and companion apps, with combined usage and server-grouped quota views.
Added browser-side server health checks, offline-friendly server setup, and automatic recovery after a server becomes reachable.
Companion settings now migrate the previous single-server preference into the multi-server format without resetting other preferences.
Sessions requests now use two-tool concurrency so one cold scan does not block the remaining tools.
Improved startup warming, stale-response refreshes, persistent session indexing, and cache compatibility across wheel restamps.
Made the active homepage date range immediately visible with a localized, keyboard-accessible range selector.
Companion apps now show multi-day quota resets in days, matching the dashboard.
